name: Cap'n Jazz
label: Jade Tree
lede: Suburban Chicago teenagers with a French horn, an a-ha cover and a 28-word album title split up in Little Rock in 1995. Nearly every band that came out of the wreckage became someone's favorite.

eras.title: Toe Jam, in the Buffalo Grove suburbs
eras.text: Two brothers and two friends in Buffalo Grove, Illinois, northwest of Chicago, start a band that sounds like their own take on Gauge and Fugazi.

years.h: Two brothers and two friends start Toe Jam in Buffalo Grove
years.p: [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]], 14 or 15, and his little brother [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]] form Toe Jam with guitarist [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] and bassist [[Sam Zurick|5a8b6d87-8e75-42a5-9a70-c03e84b22b67]]. The name changes to Cap'n Jazz soon after.
years.xp: Mike took over the drums at 12, after the original drummer quit to concentrate on football. He learned on a 16-piece kit.

eras.title: One album, a 28-word title, and a breakup on tour
eras.text: With Davey von Bohlen on second guitar, Cap'n Jazz put out singles, compilation tracks and a single album. By the time anyone noticed it, the band was gone.

years.h: A comp track and an Underdog 7-inch with a very long title
years.p: Cap'n Jazz appears on the Further Beyond compilation Boys 16 to 18 Years... Age of Action, then puts out the Sometimes if you stand further away from something... 7-inch on Underdog Records.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen joins on guitar and backing vocals
years.p: [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]] completes the five-piece that most fans mean when they say Cap'n Jazz.

yt: Knights of Columbus Hall, Arlington Heights, c. 1995
years.h: Shmap'n Shmazz, the album whose real title takes a breath
years.p: Cap'n Jazz's only album is officially Burritos, Inspiration Point, Fork Balloon Sports, Cards in the Spokes, Automatic Biographies, Kites, Kung Fu, Trophies, Banana Peels We've Slipped On and Egg Shells We've Tippy Toed Over. The CD printed Shmap'n Shmazz on top.
years.xp: The album came out on Man With Gun Records. Fans know the band mostly through the Jade Tree anthology that followed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cap'n Jazz · Wikipedia: Tim Kinsella · Wikipedia: Analphabetapolothology
years.h: Nine days into a summer tour, Cap'n Jazz is over
years.p: After a show at Das Yutes a Go-Go in Little Rock, Arkansas, the band splits. Davey von Bohlen goes home to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]] full-time.
years.xp: Tim Kinsella's Wikipedia entry dates the last show to July 14, 1995. Two songs from it, Forget Who We Are and Olerud, turn up on Analphabetapolothology.

years.h: Tim Kinsella starts Joan of Arc the same year
years.p: From the wreckage [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]] forms [[Joan of Arc|0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee]], which he fronts for the next 25 years.

eras.title: Spread thin, then collected
eras.text: Cap'n Jazz grows after it ends. Its members land in Joan of Arc, The Promise Ring and American Football, and a Jade Tree double CD hands the catalog to people who never saw a show.

years.p: [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]] forms [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]] with Steve Lamos and Steve Holmes. The band's one album arrives in 1999.

years.big: "I realized I named it wrong. It was already printed."
years.h: Analphabetapolothology packs Cap'n Jazz onto two Jade Tree CDs
years.p: Tim Kinsella on the title he typed in at a Madison, Wisconsin, shop. Ninety-nine minutes: the album, singles, comp tracks, demos and an [[a-ha|7364dea6-ca9a-48e3-be01-b44ad0d19897]] Take On Me cover. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp:
The intended title was Anthroalphabetapolothology, pronounced an alphabet apolo(tholo)gy. Kinsella drove to Madison, typed it in, and caught the error after it was printed.

The set runs 36 tracks across two discs, with everything except an early song called Naive.

years.h: Owls: Cap'n Jazz minus von Bohlen
years.p: The Kinsellas, Victor Villarreal and Sam Zurick sign to Jade Tree as [[Owls|f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2]] on May 3, 2001, and record an album with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The band lasts one tour.

eras.title: A reunion nobody planned on
eras.text: Fifteen years after Little Rock, Cap'n Jazz plays again, first as a surprise and then on festival stages. They return in 2017 and 2024, the last time for the album's 30th anniversary.

years.h: A surprise Cap'n Jazz set interrupts a variety show
years.p: At the Empty Bottle in Chicago, during Joan of Arc's Don't Mind Control Variety Show, Cap'n Jazz plays an impromptu set.

years.cap: Cap'n Jazz at the Starlight Ballroom, Philadelphia, 2010
years.h: Forecastle in Louisville is the first official reunion show
years.p: The five-piece plays Forecastle in Kentucky. Chicago's Bottom Lounge show sells out in 48 hours, so they add a second night.
years.xp: The Chicago shows marked a vinyl reissue of Analphabetapolothology. More US dates followed that summer and fall.

years.h: Cousin Nate Kinsella takes von Bohlen's guitar
years.p: [[Nate Kinsella|dee29ad9-ba52-4af1-8372-4acbfb725554]] plays second guitar at FYF Fest in Los Angeles, Riot Fest in Chicago, and dates in San Francisco, New York and London.

years.h: Empty Bottle again, then Las Vegas five days later
years.p: Cap'n Jazz reunites in Chicago and plays Best Friends Forever Fest in Las Vegas on the next weekend.

years.h: Shmap'n Shmazz turns 30 and sells out San Francisco
years.p: On an anniversary tour with Coffin Prick, Cap'n Jazz sells out the Great American Music Hall. One review noted fans young enough to be Tim Kinsella's kids.
